findings.title: Backup codes cannot be used by OAuth users in the external TOTP flow
findings.body: The condition `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)` throws `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` when no TOTP code is provided. When an OAuth user (Google/SAML) with 2FA enabled uses the external TOTP flow (redirected to `/auth/login?totp=...`) and chooses to use a backup code instead, `credentials.totpCode` is empty, so this check incorrectly rejects the request. The condition should also account for `credentials.backupCode`, e.g., `!credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode`. The same issue affects lines 117 and 121 where `!credentials.totpCode` is used to gate password verification.

findings.title: Toggle and Cancel buttons inside form lack type="button" and may trigger form submission
findings.body: The 'Lost access'/'Go back' toggle button (line 116) and the 'Cancel' button (line 122) are rendered inside a `<Form>` component but do not specify `type="button"` and do not call `e.preventDefault()`. HTML buttons default to `type="submit"`, so clicking either button will also trigger form submission (calling `handleDisable`) in addition to their onClick handlers. Compare with `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` where backup-code step buttons explicitly call `e.preventDefault()`. This can cause unexpected API calls and error messages when the user only intends to toggle the input mode or cancel.

findings.title: twoFactorLostAccess state is not reset when the modal is cancelled
findings.body: When the user clicks 'Cancel' (line 122, calling `onCancel`), the `twoFactorLostAccess` state remains `true` if it was toggled. The next time the modal is opened, it will display the backup code input instead of the TOTP input, which is unexpected. The `resetForm` helper clears field values and error message but does not reset `twoFactorLostAccess`. The state should be reset either in `onCancel` or when the dialog's `open` prop transitions to true.

findings.title: Object URL for backup codes download is never revoked on unmount
findings.body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` is called at line 99 to create a download link for backup codes. `URL.revokeObjectURL` is only called if a new setup is initiated (line 98 checks `if (backupCodesUrl)`). If the component unmounts (e.g., user navigates away) without re-initiating setup, the object URL is leaked. A `useEffect` cleanup should revoke the URL on unmount.

findings.title: Backup code comparison uses non-constant-time indexOf
findings.body: The backup code check `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` at line 144 (and similarly in `disable.ts` line 61) uses `Array.indexOf`, which short-circuits on the first match. This is not a constant-time comparison, theoretically allowing timing-based side-channel attacks to guess backup codes character by character. While the practical risk is low (codes are random hex, single-use, and behind rate limiting), using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for each comparison would be a defense-in-depth improvement consistent with security best practices for authentication code verification.

findings.title: No end-to-end test for logging in with a backup code
findings.body: The PR description states backup codes can be used during login via 'Lost access', and the TODO at line 12 acknowledges this gap. There is no test that verifies a user can actually authenticate using a backup code, nor that a used backup code is invalidated (set to null) and cannot be reused. This is the core security property of the feature and should be tested before merge.
